Census Income Dataset Analysis

Executive Summary

This report presents a comprehensive analysis of the Census Income dataset, containing 48,842 records with demographic and income information. The analysis explores various factors that influence whether an individual's annual income exceeds 50K, including age, education, occupation, work hours, and other demographic characteristics.

Key Findings:

  • 76.1% of individuals earn ≤50K, while 23.9% earn 50K
  • High earners are on average 7.4 years older, have 2 more years of education, and work 6.7 more hours per week
  • A logistic regression model achieved 81.5% accuracy with an AUC-ROC of 0.831
  • Education and capital gains are the strongest predictors of high income

Income Distribution Analysis

分析问题
  • What percentage of the population earns over 50K?
  • How does income vary across different demographic groups?

The dataset shows a significant class imbalance with 76.1% of individuals earning ≤50K and only 23.9% earning 50K. This imbalance is typical for income prediction tasks and was accounted for in model training.

The analysis reveals a gender gap in high-income earners. While males have a higher proportion earning 50K, females are also represented in the high-income bracket, particularly in professional and executive roles.

Age Analysis:

High-income earners tend to be older, with the distribution showing that income 50K becomes more common starting around age 35 and peaks in the 45-55 range. The average age for high earners is 44.3 years compared to 36.9 years for those earning ≤50K.

Education Impact on Income

分析问题
  • How does education level correlate with income?
  • Which education levels are most likely to earn over 50K?

Education is one of the strongest predictors of income in this dataset. Individuals with higher education levels show significantly higher rates of earning 50K.

education_by_income.json
asset

Key Education Insights:

1. Advanced Degrees: Masters, Doctorate, and Professional School graduates have the highest rates of earning 50K

2. Bachelor's Degree: Strong predictor of high income, with over 40% of holders earning 50K

3. High School Graduates: Lower likelihood of high income, but still represent a significant portion of 50K earners

4. No High School: Very low probability of earning 50K

The average education years for high earners is 11.6 years compared to 9.6 years for those earning ≤50K.

Predictive Modeling

分析问题

Model Performance

A logistic regression model was trained using numeric features age, education years, capital gain, capital loss, hours per week to predict whether an individual earns 50K.

Model Metrics:

  • Accuracy: 81.5%
  • AUC-ROC: 0.831

The ROC curve shows good discriminatory power, with the model significantly outperforming random classification.

Key Insights and Recommendations

分析问题
  • What are the main drivers of high income in this dataset?
  • How can this analysis be used for policy or business decisions?

Summary of Key Findings

1. Education is Critical: Each additional year of education significantly increases the likelihood of earning 50K

2. Age Matters: Income typically increases with age, peaking in mid-to-late 40s

3. Capital Investments Matter: Those with capital gains are much more likely to be high earners

4. Work Effort Pays Off: Longer work hours correlate with higher income

5. Career Choice is Important: Executive and professional roles offer the highest income potential

6. Marriage Correlation: Married individuals, particularly those in stable marriages, show higher incomes

Limitations

  • Temporal Constraints: Data represents a specific time period and may not reflect current economic conditions
  • Class Imbalance: The 76/24 split affects model performance and interpretation
  • Limited Features: Important factors like location, industry, and company size are not included
  • Self-Reported Data: Potential biases in self-reported information

Recommendations

For Individuals:

  • Invest in education and skill development
  • Consider career paths in executive or professional roles
  • Focus on long-term career building over short-term gains
  • Consider the value of capital investments and savings

For Policymakers:

  • Continue supporting education programs to boost income potential
  • Address the income gap through targeted policies
  • Support programs that help workers transition to higher-paying occupations

For Researchers:

  • Collect additional features like industry and location
  • Implement techniques to handle class imbalance
  • Explore non-linear models random forests, gradient boosting
  • Conduct longitudinal studies to track income progression

Conclusion

This analysis of the Census Income dataset reveals clear patterns in the factors that influence whether individuals earn more than 50K annually. Education, age, capital gains, and work hours emerge as the strongest predictors. The logistic regression model achieves good predictive accuracy 81.5%, demonstrating that income can be reasonably predicted from demographic and employment characteristics.

The insights from this analysis can inform career planning, educational investments, and policy decisions aimed at improving income outcomes. Future work could explore more complex models and additional features to improve prediction accuracy and uncover deeper insights.
